The second proposed trait assignment approach, ‘Blast Neighbourhood’ (pseudocode in Box S1), was similarity-based and analogous to an established method in taxonomic profiling (Figure S3), that is, assignment of the intersection of characters possessed by reference neighbours, as defined by sequence similarity between pairs (Meier et al., 2006; Tanabe & Toju, 2013).

The COI DNA barcode region (\~650 bp) was amplified; whole genomic DNA was extracted with DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kits (QIAGEN GmbH, Hilden, Germany) and COI amplified using several universal primer pairs.
It is therefore broadly applicable to any homologous barcodes and metabarcodes, while still permitting integration of taxon-associated trait data in cases those taxa can be tied to barcode sequences.

basisOfRecord.quote: We built a novel dataset of traits and DNA barcodes for wild bees in China.
For Phylogenetic Assignment, we additionally conducted a species-level analysis of publically available bee trait data.

We used bee specimens and COI sequences from four locations in China (Figure S1); specimens were newly collected and sequenced at three locations, while those of Xishuangbanna were collected and sequenced earlier as described in (Liu et al., 2017).
To collect a diverse set of bee species, we used blind sweep net and yellow pan traps around flowers (McCravy et al., 2019).

We built one of the first specimen-level insect datasets that comprise both DNA barcodes and traits and use it to assess three proposed approaches to taxon-independent assignment of functional traits to query DNA barcodes (overview in Figure 1).

We also collated species-level trait data from the literature and used this to practically estimate levels of state assignment for a wide range of informative traits, given the structural characteristics of each.
Phylogeny includes reference species derived from mined DNA barcodes, and queries which are denoted by red circles at tips.
TA B L E 1 Phylogenetic prediction for a wide range of traits (including both those newly measured herein and collated from the literature) conducted on a collated set of bee MOTU.
